record.paper_title: Selected Conjectures and Open Problems on Directed Graphs
record.original_question: For a tournament, meaning an orientation of a complete graph, that contains at least one directed cycle, is there always an arc whose reversal decreases the total number of directed cycles?

evidence.quote: which claims that every oriented graph (i.e., a digraph without cycles of length 2), which has a cycle (in this paper all cycles and paths in digraphs are directed), contains an arc whose reversal decreases the number of cycles.
However, the conjecture restricted to tournaments, posed by Reid and Beineke [63] in 1978, remains open.
An orientation of a complete graph is called a tournament

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A tournament is an orientation of a finite complete graph; that is, a directed graph obtained by assigning a direction to every edge of a complete graph. A directed cycle in a tournament is a sequence of distinct vertices v_1, v_2, …, v_k, v_1 (k ≥ 3) such that each consecutive pair forms an arc in the tournament. Given a tournament T that contains at least one directed cycle, the reversal of an arc (u,v) is the operation of replacing (u,v) by (v,u), producing a new tournament T'. Let c(T) denote the total number of directed cycles in T (of all lengths).

Prove or disprove: for every tournament T with c(T) ≥ 1, there exists an arc e of T whose reversal yields a tournament T' with c(T') < c(T).
artifact.status_search_result: Ádám's original conjecture for general digraphs has known counterexamples, but the restriction to tournaments, posed by Reid and Beineke in 1978, is reported as still open in surveys on tournament problems. Recent work (e.g., a 2017 master's thesis on Ádám's conjecture and arc-reversal problems, and surveys by Bang-Jensen and Gutin) treats the tournament version as an unresolved problem, verifying partial cases (e.g., quasi-acyclic digraphs, certain connectivity classes).

status_evidence.title: Ádám's Conjecture and Arc Reversal Problems (Salas, thesis)
status_evidence.snippet: Investigates Ádám's conjecture and its restriction to tournaments, discussing partial results and counterexamples for general digraphs.
status_evidence.claim: The tournament version of Ádám's conjecture is studied as an unresolved problem with only partial results.

status_evidence.title: Problems and conjectures concerning connectivity, paths, trees and cycles in tournament-like digraphs
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of open problems on tournaments including Reid–Beineke arc-reversal conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture restricted to tournaments remains listed among open problems.

status_evidence.title: Paths, Trees and Cycles in Tournaments (Bang-Jensen, Gutin)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey mentioning Ádám's conjecture for tournaments as open.
status_evidence.claim: Authoritative survey lists the tournament restriction of Ádám's conjecture as open.
